page: Microsoft Azure B2ats_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Basv2 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with a base clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads, supported by 1.0 GB of system memory. The processor features a 32 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, but it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reflect the burstable nature and resource constraints of this instance. Single-core CPU performance is strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2701.19, placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak at 2701.19, and the Passmark CPU score of 3130.58 is also in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is limited, with a cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth of 140.76 GB/sec and a poor Passmark memory score. Database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the bottom 10%, as does the static web serving throughput of 2.77 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B2ats_v2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require continuous full CPU utilization. The burstable CPU allocation model allows users to pay a lower baseline rate while retaining the ability to handle occasional spikes in demand. Due to the tiny 1.0 GB memory capacity and weak multi-core performance, this server is best suited for lightweight, non-resource-intensive workloads. Appropriate use cases include low-traffic web serving, basic microservices, development or testing environments, and simple automation scripts that can operate within strict memory limits.
